question: Billed Workers Standard Requests (Workers + Pages Functions) were about 1,600 on 2026-09-25, against about 1,060 on a typical day the week before. Why?

steps.query: SELECT date, SUM(requests) AS workers_requests, SUM(errors) AS workers_errors FROM workers_daily GROUP BY date ORDER BY date

steps.purpose: Quantify resource-level change versus seven preceding days and errors
steps.query: WITH w AS (SELECT worker resource, SUM(CASE WHEN date BETWEEN '2026-09-18' AND '2026-09-24' THEN requests ELSE 0 END)/7.0 avg_prev, SUM(CASE WHEN date='2026-09-25' THEN requests ELSE 0 END) today, SUM(CASE WHEN date='2026-09-25' THEN errors ELSE 0 END) errors_today FROM workers_daily GROUP BY worker), f AS (SELECT project resource, SUM(CASE WHEN date BETWEEN '2026-09-18' AND '2026-09-24' THEN requests ELSE 0 END)/7.0 avg_prev, SUM(CASE WHEN date='2026-09-25' THEN requests ELSE 0 END) today, SUM(CASE WHEN date='2026-09-25' THEN errors ELSE 0 END) errors_today FROM functions_daily GROUP BY project) SELECT 'worker' kind,resource,avg_prev,today,errors_today FROM w WHERE avg_prev>0 OR today>0 UNION ALL SELECT 'function',resource,avg_prev,today,errors_today FROM f WHERE avg_prev>0 OR today>0 ORDER BY today DESC

finding.summary: The cause of the full-day increase is undetermined. Billed usage was 1,592 on 2026-09-25 versus a 1,061/day average over 2026-09-18–24; the clearest outlier was 351 ops-console Pages Function requests in the single minute 20:12 UTC (354 total that day), but the available Functions data cannot show their hostname, paths, or clients. Blog also ran above its prior-week average, with zone traffic showing scanner-like activity on its mapped hosts, but that does not explain the separate ops-console minute burst.
finding.where: Account-wide, 2026-09-25 UTC day: ops-console Pages Function, especially 20:12 UTC; blog Worker activity concentrated at 01:00 and 04:00 UTC. Total billed requests: 1,592 vs 1,061/day average for 2026-09-18–24.

evidence.fact: Summed Workers and Pages Functions requests were 1,592 on 2026-09-25; the seven preceding days summed to 7,429, or 1,061.3/day.

ops-console recorded 354 Pages Function requests on 2026-09-25 versus 21.7/day over 2026-09-18–24. functions_minute attributes 351 of the 354 to pages-worker--100007-production at 20:12 UTC; resources maps that script ID to the ops-console Pages project. Errors were zero that day.

blog recorded 1,228 Worker requests versus a 1,023/day average over the preceding seven days. workers_hourly shows 473 at 01:00 and 550 at 04:00 UTC, with zero errors; hosts maps blog to blog.acme.example and blog.northwind.example.

At 01:00 and 04:00 UTC, zone_requests for the mapped blog hosts included concentrated probing from individual client IP hashes, including 404s and some firewallManaged blocks; this is scanner-like zone traffic concurrent with the blog Worker bursts, but zone traffic also includes requests not billed as code executions.
No deployment of blog or ops-console is recorded near the increase; the latest recorded blog entries are secret changes on 2026-09-17, and the recorded ops-console deployments are from 2026-06-16.

ruled_out.suspect: A deploy or launch caused the increase
ruled_out.why: Neither of the principal resources has a deployment recorded near 2026-09-25, and both had prior usage; the recorded ops-console deployments are from June.

ruled_out.suspect: Errors or retries/loops explain the rise
ruled_out.why: workers_daily and functions_daily show zero errors for the leading resources on 2026-09-25. This does not rule out application-level retries that are not represented as errors.

ruled_out.suspect: The ops.acme.example scanner traffic at 22:00 UTC explains the 20:12 ops-console Functions burst
ruled_out.why: zone_requests shows credential/config probing at 22:00, not at the Functions burst time; Functions analytics cannot establish that the 20:12 requests came through this hostname. Traffic via the project's pages.dev hostname is not present in zone data.

gaps: Functions analytics has no path, client, user-agent, or hostname detail, so the cause and source of the 351-request ops-console minute cannot be determined from this collection.
zone_requests includes static requests and requests stopped by Cloudflare; it cannot prove which blog requests invoked code. It also omits *.pages.dev traffic.

The data does not establish whether the ops-console burst was human traffic, a bot, a scheduled task, or app behavior; application logs or request-level Pages telemetry for 20:12 UTC would settle this.
finding.impact: About 531 more billed requests than the prior-week daily average (roughly 50%); errors were not elevated. The blog host data shows scanner-like probing, including attempts against paths that returned 404 or were blocked, so review protections, but the largest single billed burst has no attributable security cause in this data.
finding.recommendation: Inspect ops-console Pages request logs or analytics around 20:12 UTC on 2026-09-25, including pages.dev traffic, route, client, and invocation origin; check scheduled-task and application logs for the same minute. For blog, review the scanner traffic and existing managed/custom firewall or rate-limit coverage, while distinguishing blocked requests from requests that invoke the Worker.
